question: How do I stop worrying about things I can't control?
html:
You stop worrying by sorting the world into two piles, what you actually control and what you don't, and then refusing to put your peace in the second pile.

The real work starts with noticing the line between your own stuff, meaning your judgments and choices, and everything else, meaning your body, your possessions, other people. Once you've actually practiced telling those apart, and you only let the first group count as "yours to worry about," there's nothing left outside you that can be taken or blocked.

When you have made this preparation, and have practised this discipline, to distinguish that which belongs to another from that which is your own, the things which are subject to hindrance from those which are not, to consider the things free from hindrance to concern yourself, and those which are not free not to concern yourself, to keep your desire steadily fixed to the things which do concern yourself, and turned from the things which do not concern yourself; do you still fear any man?

Epictetus, The Discourses, A SELECTION FROM THE DISCOURSES OF EPICTETUS, para. 197

and what else have you been studying from the beginning than to distinguish between your own and not your own, the things which are in your power and not in your power, the things subject to hindrance and not subject?

Epictetus, The Discourses, A SELECTION FROM THE DISCOURSES OF EPICTETUS, para. 197

That same sorting is what gets you through an actual hard moment, like standing in front of a judge. If what you care about is keeping a will in line with nature, you already have every advantage, because no one can touch that part of you no matter what verdict comes down.

OF TRANQUILLITY (FREEDOM FROM PERTURBATION).—Consider, you who are going into court, what you wish to maintain and what you wish to succeed in. For if you wish to maintain a will conformable to nature, you have every security, every facility, you have no troubles.

Epictetus, The Discourses, A SELECTION FROM THE DISCOURSES OF EPICTETUS, para. 67

There's a second way to put it, which is less about sorting and more about where you stand. Find your own center and stay there, instead of handing that ground over to whatever happens to be bothering you. The way you find that center is by resting in your connection to something larger than yourself and staying in that awareness.

To live undisturbed by passing occurrences you must first find your own centre.

Ralph Waldo Trine, In Tune with the Infinite, FULLNESS OF LIFE, BODILY HEALTH AND VIGOR, para. 50

Find your centre and live in it.

Ralph Waldo Trine, In Tune with the Infinite, FULLNESS OF LIFE, BODILY HEALTH AND VIGOR, para. 50

By realizing his oneness with the Infinite Power, and by living continually in this realization.

Ralph Waldo Trine, In Tune with the Infinite, FULLNESS OF LIFE, BODILY HEALTH AND VIGOR, para. 50
